You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "# Continual-ARC task-6c7ae49f: two-band recoloring

## Rule observed
Input consists of a random binary mask/top field (0/1), a single horizontal separator row (color 6 or 4), and a lower 7-row picture using background color 9/8 and foreground 0/7/6. Output is the lower picture only, but recolored by combining it with the top mask: output dimensions are 7 x grid width. The lower picture's background remains 0. At each coordinate, output is color 2 iff the lower cell is foreground-colored (not its background color) AND the corresponding top mask cell is 1; otherwise output 0. In the solved instance, lower field had 9 as its background and 0 as the marks; output retained the marks at locations where the matching top cell was 1, recoloring them to 2.

## Demonstrations
Demo 1: input 15x27. Upper mask is rows 0-6 (background 8, holes 0); row 7 separator 9; lower rows 8-14 (background 0, foreground 7). Output is 7x27. Output 2s correspond exactly to lower foreground 7s that align with upper-mask background 8 (i.e. upper cell is NOT the hole 0); all other cells are 0. Thus keep lower foreground only where top-mask cell is nonzero.

Demo 2: input 15x24. Upper mask rows 0-6 with 1 background and 0 holes; row 7 separator 4; lower rows 8-14 with background 6 and holes/foreground 0. Output 7x24 is the complement picture: output 2 at lower cells that are 0 AND corresponding upper cell is 1; output 0 at lower 6s or when upper cell is 0.

These demos establish the general rule: two 7-row binary patterns are combined by AND of the upper rows' nonzero status and the lower rows' non-background/foreground status, then written as 2; keep lower image row order and width. Ignore separator.

## Solved instance
Test upper 3 rows, separator row color 6, lower 3 rows (pad/paired top rows only 3), width 27. Lower background=9, marks=0. Output was 3x27 and was correctly submitted as:
[2,2,0,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,0,2,0,2,2,2,0,0,2,2,2,2,2,2,0,2]
[2,2,2,2,2,0,2,2,0,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,0,2,2,2,0,2]
[2,2,2,2,2,2,0,2,2,2,2,2,0,2,2,0,2,2,2,2,0,2,2,0,2,2,2]

## Pitfalls / scoring insight
The top band is a mask, not part of output. Output is the lower band dimensions, not necessarily all input rows and not necessarily three rows. Use the top mask's nonzero cells to select the lower foreground marks. The first two attempts wrongly ignored the mask and output only lower marks; that was incorrect. No need for extra demos once this rule is recognized.
